title: Customs Duty Exemption and Tariff Amendment Procedures
summary: This thread tracks the evolution of SRO-based amendments to customs duty tables and tariff structures. Over time, the legal basis for these amendments shifted from the Value Added Tax Act, 1991 to the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012, reflecting broader legislative updates in the Bangladeshi tax regime.

evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from VAT Act 1991 to VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
evolution.scope: Continuous refinement of HS codes and tariff descriptions for customs duty adjustments.

timeline.change: Amendment of existing SRO using VAT Act 1991 authority.
Replacement of existing table entries under Customs Act 1969 and VAT Act 1991.
Further modification of tariff headings and HS codes.
Shift in legal basis to VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.

Customs Act 1969: This act provides the enabling legal authority under section 20 for the government to issue this amendment notification in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(2) of this act is cited as a source of legal authority for the issuance of this amendment notification.
National Board of Revenue: The government is mandated to consult with this body before issuing notifications that amend existing customs or tax-related orders.
S.R.O. 11-AIN/2005: This specific earlier notification is being formally amended by the present order to update various H.S. Code entries listed in its schedule.
H.S. Code: The order corrects and replaces several specified H.S. Code classifications within the 'Part A' table of an existing notification to ensure tariff consistency and accuracy.

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act grants the government the authority to issue notifications and amend existing customs orders in the public interest.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act provides legal authority for the government, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue, to issue regulatory notifications regarding taxes.
National Board of Revenue: The board is the designated authority that must be consulted by the government before issuing or amending regulatory notifications under customs and VAT laws.
S.R.O. 154-AIN/2016: This previous regulatory notification is amended by replacing its existing table with a new table to reflect updated customs classifications or provisions.
TABLE: This table identifies specific goods by H.S. Code and description that are subject to revised regulatory treatment, including various industrial and agricultural machinery parts such as pipes, transmission belts, engine parts, and specialized gauges.
H.S. Code: The table lists specific codes to precisely identify items including transmission belts, diesel engine parts for agricultural use, fasteners, and specialized industrial components for customs assessment purposes.

Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the government to make specific regulatory amendments in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The Board acts as the consultative body for the government in issuing notifications and amending existing customs and taxation orders.
S.R.O. 150-AIN/2013/2437/Customs: This existing notification is being amended by the current order to update specific H.S. Code entries within its associated table.

TABLE: The table attached to the original S.R.O. is modified to substitute descriptive entries for specific H.S. Codes, ensuring accurate categorization of imported goods.

এস,আর,ও নং ১৪৮-আইন/২০২২/৯৬/কাস্টমস।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 19 এর sub-section (1) এবং মূল্য সংযোজন কর ও সম্পূরক শুল্ক আইন, ২০১২ (২০১২ সনের ৪৭ নং আইন) এর ধারা ১২৬ এর উপ-ধারা (১) এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে সরকার, জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ডের সহিত পরামর্শক্রমে, ২৪ মে, ২০২১ খ্রিস্টাব্দ মোতাবেক ১০ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪২৮ তারিখে জারীকৃত প্রজ্ঞাপন এস,আর,ও নং ১২০-আইন/২০২১/০৯/কাস্টমস এর নিম্নরূপ অধিকতর সংশোধন করিল, যথা:-

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act provides the government with the authority to issue notifications, including those that amend or rescind previous customs orders, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: Section 126(1) of this Act provides the legal basis and authority for the government to issue notifications related to customs and taxation adjustments.
National Board of Revenue: The government is mandated to consult with this body when exercising its legal authority to issue or amend customs notifications.
S.R.O. 120-AIN/2021: This existing customs notification, originally issued in May 2021, is subject to further amendment by the current order.
